name: Keep the sketch small
rule: Generate no more than 16 bars and exactly three tracks: Bass, Drums and Pad.

name: Separate harmony and rhythm edits
rule: Harmony suggestions may alter chord pitches or voicings. Rhythm-only suggestions change onset/duration only and preserve note counts, pitches, velocities, onset bars and ordered Pad chord groups.

name: Resolve intentionally
rule: When a progression loops, provide a clear return to tonic or explain the non-tonic loop.

name: Offer alternatives, do not overwrite
rule: Return at least two candidates when practical. Preserve original until explicit apply.

name: Source-aware recommendations
rule: Cite knowledge record IDs. Distinguish sourced theory from project heuristics and generated suggestions.

name: Do not map chord progressions to mood as fixed rules
rule: Treat genre and mood tags as tendencies tied to a cited source or listening example. A chord progression alone does not guarantee a mood or genre.

source.title: おしゃれコード進行一覧 — ジャンル別の解説
source.author: SRM.

notes: Genre descriptions in SRM are qualitative; the Kawase study also tests chord progression, tempo and rhythmic patterns together rather than treating harmony alone as the full cause.

name: Avoid arbitrary microtiming
rule: For rhythm transformations, preserve a straight baseline and create controlled, track-specific timing variants. Do not randomize all note onsets or exaggerate swing without a listening comparison.

source.title: Microtiming Deviations and Swing Feel in Jazz
source.author: George Datseris et al.

notes: Research is about jazz swing; use it as a caution about timing exaggeration, not as a universal genre formula.

name: Specify harmonic rhythm as well as chord identity
rule: When proposing a progression, state how long each chord lasts and where changes occur. A passing ii or subV should be shorter than the chord it approaches when that is the intended effect.

source.title: おしゃれコード進行一覧 — ジャンル別の解説
source.author: SRM.

notes: Based on SRM's discussion of harmonic rhythm and short inserted chords.

name: Keep reharmonization selective
rule: Start from a clear diatonic or familiar progression. Add only the substitutions, borrowed chords or passing chords that serve the section's purpose; compare against the unmodified version.

source.title: おしゃれコード進行一覧 — ジャンル別の解説
source.author: SRM.

notes: SRM cautions against overcomplicating progressions and recommends keeping a diatonic base.
